questionText: Confidential Information includes all non-public information accessed during engagement. Which of the following can be considered as confidential information?
correctAnswerText: Customer and personal data

questionText: Confidential Information includes which system-related data?
optionA: ERP/IFS Cloud data, CRIMs, integrations, and system architecture
correctAnswerText: ERP/IFS Cloud data, CRIMs, integrations, and system architecture

questionText: Confidential Information includes all non-public information accessed during engagement. Who owns all Confidential Information?
optionD: No one; it is open information
correctAnswerText: SEBSA or its customers

questionText: The Individual shall use Confidential Information:
optionC: To share with friends for feedback
correctAnswerText: Only for authorized work purposes

questionText: Which of the following is an obligation the Individual agrees to?
optionA: Access only information necessary for assigned tasks
optionB: Access all systems regardless of task relevance
optionC: Share credentials with teammates for convenience
optionD: Store data on any external device
correctAnswerText: Access only information necessary for assigned tasks

questionText: How long do confidentiality obligations survive after termination of engagement?
correctAnswerText: Indefinitely

questionText: Which of the following is prohibited?
optionA: Using approved systems and communication channels
optionB: Unauthorized copying, extraction, or storage of data
correctAnswerText: Unauthorized copying, extraction, or storage of data

questionText: The Individual shall process personal data:
optionA: Under any instructions received from anyone
correctAnswerText: Only under authorized instructions

questionText: Which data protection principle must be applied at all times?
correctAnswerText: Data minimization

questionText: What must the Individual do immediately upon suspecting a data breach?
optionA: Ignore it if it seems minor
optionC: Wait for the next audit cycle
correctAnswerText: Report it immediately

questionText: Cross-border transfers of personal data are permitted only through:
optionA: Any transfer method chosen by the Individual
optionB: Approved contractual safeguards and legal mechanisms
correctAnswerText: Approved contractual safeguards and legal mechanisms

questionText: Activities involving personal data may be subject to:
optionB: Monitoring, logging, audit verification, and security review
correctAnswerText: Monitoring, logging, audit verification, and security review

questionText: SEBSA provides services to customers operating in multiple jurisdictions, including:
correctAnswerText: The European Union

questionText: When SEBSA processes personal data on behalf of a customer, processing is governed by:
correctAnswerText: Data Processing Agreements (DPAs)

questionText: What must the Individual do regarding personal data under a Data Processing Agreement (DPA)?
optionA: Access, use, disclose, modify, transfer, and retain data only per the DPA's instructions and purposes
optionB: Use the data for any purpose they choose
optionC: Share the data with any interested party
optionD: Ignore the DPA if it seems outdated
correctAnswerText: Access, use, disclose, modify, transfer, and retain data only per the DPA's instructions and purposes

questionText: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), apply specifically to:
correctAnswerText: International/cross-border transfers of personal data

questionText: SCCs are particularly relevant for transfers between the European Union and:
optionB: Countries outside the European Economic Area
correctAnswerText: Countries outside the European Economic Area

questionText: Technical and Organizational Measures (TOMs), may include:
optionA: Access controls, authentication mechanisms, and encryption requirements
correctAnswerText: Access controls, authentication mechanisms, and encryption requirements

questionText: Which regulation is explicitly named as an applicable data protection law?
optionC: Only local Sri Lankan tax law
correctAnswerText: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)

questionText: Failure to comply with applicable data protection requirements may result in:
optionB: Disciplinary action, withdrawal of access, termination, legal proceedings, or regulatory reporting
optionC: A verbal warning only, with no further action
correctAnswerText: Disciplinary action, withdrawal of access, termination, legal proceedings, or regulatory reporting

questionText: Processing of personal, business, or system-related data during engagement is based on:
optionA: Personal consent of the Individual alone
optionB: Contractual necessity, legal obligations, and legitimate operational requirements
correctAnswerText: Contractual necessity, legal obligations, and legitimate operational requirements

questionText: Is personal consent required or relied upon for processing data necessary for employment or service delivery?
optionB: No, it is not required or relied upon
correctAnswerText: No, it is not required or relied upon

questionText: Permissions granted to an employee under the NDA signed by an employee are:
optionA: Personal consent that overrides contractual obligations
optionB: Operational in nature and not personal consent that can override contractual obligations
correctAnswerText: Operational in nature and not personal consent that can override contractual obligations

questionText: Does an attempt to withdraw consent affect the validity of the NDA?
optionA: Yes, it fully cancels the Agreement
optionB: No, it does not affect the validity or the Individual's obligations
optionC: Yes, but only for one month
optionD: It depends on the Individual's job title
correctAnswerText: No, it does not affect the validity or the Individual's obligations

questionText: The Individual's access to systems, data, or environments is based on:
correctAnswerText: Role-based authorization, not personal consent

questionText: Can SEBSA continue to process and retain data after withdrawal of consent is communicated?
optionA: No, SEBSA must stop immediately in all cases
optionB: Yes, where necessary for business continuity, legal compliance, audit, or security obligations
optionC: Only if the Individual approves in writing
correctAnswerText: Yes, where necessary for business continuity, legal compliance, audit, or security obligations

questionText: Does termination of employment equate to withdrawal of data processing obligations?
optionB: No, especially where retention or processing is required by law or contract
correctAnswerText: No, especially where retention or processing is required by law or contract

questionText: SEBSA may engage subcontractors or third-party service providers only where:
optionA: The Individual personally approves it informally
optionB: Permitted under the applicable customer agreement, and with customer approval where required
optionC: No approval is needed at all
optionD: A third party requests it directly
correctAnswerText: Permitted under the applicable customer agreement, and with customer approval where required

questionText: The Individual shall NOT share customer systems, credentials, or data with:
optionB: Any third party or person outside the authorized project team without prior written authorization
correctAnswerText: Any third party or person outside the authorized project team without prior written authorization

questionText: Does the restriction on sharing customer access apply to other SEBSA group entities and employees not authorized for that project?
optionA: No, internal SEBSA staff are always exempt
optionB: Yes, the restriction applies equally to them
optionD: Only during the first month of engagement
correctAnswerText: Yes, the restriction applies equally to them

questionText: Unauthorized sharing of customer access or data with colleagues on different customer accounts is considered:
optionB: A serious breach of confidentiality, data protection, and security obligations
optionC: Acceptable if done to help a colleague
correctAnswerText: A serious breach of confidentiality, data protection, and security obligations

questionText: Which of the following is a mandatory security requirement?
optionA: Use only SEBSA-approved systems and devices
optionB: Use any personal device for convenience
correctAnswerText: Use only SEBSA-approved systems and devices

questionText: Is the Individual permitted to install unauthorized software or tools?
correctAnswerText: No, this is prohibited

questionText: Sharing of credentials under any circumstance is:
correctAnswerText: Never permitted

questionText: Under Information Security and Access Control Obligations, what access principle must be followed by an individual?
correctAnswerText: Least-privilege access

questionText: Under Incident Reporting and Responsibility, which of the following must be immediately reported by the Individual?
correctAnswerText: Unauthorized access or data exposure

questionText: Loss or compromise of devices or credentials should be:
optionD: Ignored if the device is later recovered
correctAnswerText: Reported immediately

questionText: Failure to report incidents in a timely manner may be treated as:
optionB: A material breach of the Agreement
correctAnswerText: A material breach of the Agreement

questionText: Which of these is a reportable incident?
optionA: Security threats, phishing, or malware activity
correctAnswerText: Security threats, phishing, or malware activity

questionText: Who owns all work products created during engagement, including code and documentation?
optionD: No one; they become public domain
correctAnswerText: SEBSA or its customers

questionText: What does the Individual do with rights, title, and interest in work created during engagement?
optionB: Irrevocably assigns them to SEBSA or the relevant customer
correctAnswerText: Irrevocably assigns them to SEBSA or the relevant customer

questionText: How long does the non-competition and non-solicitation restriction last after termination?
correctAnswerText: Twelve (12) months

questionText: Which activity is restricted during and after employment?
optionA: Engaging in competing services with SEBSA customers or competitors
correctAnswerText: Engaging in competing services with SEBSA customers or competitors

questionText: If the Individual receives an external approach to solicit SEBSA employees or customers, they must:
optionA: Handle it independently without informing anyone
optionB: Immediately report it to SEBSA management
correctAnswerText: Immediately report it to SEBSA management

questionText: Soliciting or recruiting SEBSA employees, contractors, or customers during the restricted period is:
correctAnswerText: Prohibited

questionText: SEBSA-provided devices and systems must be used:
correctAnswerText: Solely for authorized business purposes

questionText: Which of the following is strictly prohibited?
optionB: Storing company or customer data on personal devices
correctAnswerText: Storing company or customer data on personal devices

questionText: Is using unauthorized cloud services or external storage permitted?
correctAnswerText: No, it is strictly prohibited

questionText: Upon termination or request, the Individual shall immediately:
optionA: Keep SEBSA property as a memento
optionB: Return all SEBSA property including devices, documents, and credentials
correctAnswerText: Return all SEBSA property including devices, documents, and credentials

questionText: What must the Individual do with SEBSA and customer data stored on any medium after termination?
optionC: Transfer it to a personal device
optionD: Share it with a new employer
correctAnswerText: Permanently delete it

questionText: What may a breach of the Agreement result in?
optionB: Disciplinary action, termination, legal proceedings, and recovery of damages
correctAnswerText: Disciplinary action, termination, legal proceedings, and recovery of damages

questionText: May SEBSA report breaches to customers or regulatory authorities?
correctAnswerText: Yes, where required

questionText: Do internal SEBSA policies and procedures remain binding even when updated periodically?
optionA: No, updates require the Individual's re-signature to be binding
optionB: Yes, they remain binding without requiring re-signature unless legally required
optionC: No, updated policies never apply retroactively
optionD: Only if approved by a court
correctAnswerText: Yes, they remain binding without requiring re-signature unless legally required

questionText: Which of the following is included among binding service delivery processes?
optionA: Incident management, change control, and escalation procedures
correctAnswerText: Incident management, change control, and escalation procedures

questionText: SEBSA may be subject to audits, assessments, and inspections conducted by:
optionB: Customers, regulators, certification bodies, or authorized representatives of SEBSA
correctAnswerText: Customers, regulators, certification bodies, or authorized representatives of SEBSA

questionText: What must the Individual do during an authorized audit or compliance review?
optionA: Provide truthful and accurate information, records, and documentation
optionD: Provide information only if it favors them
correctAnswerText: Provide truthful and accurate information, records, and documentation

questionText: What may providing false or misleading information during an audit constitute?
optionB: A serious breach of the Agreement
correctAnswerText: A serious breach of the Agreement

questionText: NDA signed by a SEBSA employee is governed by the laws applicable to:
optionB: The SEBSA entity under which the Individual is engaged
correctAnswerText: The SEBSA entity under which the Individual is engaged

questionText: Which jurisdictions are mentioned as possible governing jurisdictions depending on contractual arrangement?
optionA: Sri Lanka, Romania, Denmark, UAE, or the United States
correctAnswerText: Sri Lanka, Romania, Denmark, UAE, or the United States

questionText: Do applicable international data protection obligations remain enforceable regardless of jurisdiction?
optionA: No, they apply only in the EU
optionB: Yes, they remain enforceable regardless of jurisdiction
optionC: Only if specified in a separate contract
correctAnswerText: Yes, they remain enforceable regardless of jurisdiction
